chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said:

I heard Al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the sun declines and you are in the city, and you intend to travel, then pray complete (Salat). But when you go out after the decline (of the sun), then shorten Al-Asr (Salat).'

key_terms.الْمِصْرُ: The city or place of residence

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler shorten their Asr prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the precise temporal boundary for the obligation of Qasr, establishing that the intent to travel must coincide with the Dhuhr prayer time while still within the city limits (Misr). It highlights the Shia juristic consensus that if one departs after Zawal (midday decline), the Asr prayer is performed as Qasr, distinguishing it from the Tamam performance of Dhuhr. This ruling underscores the importance of the 'time of prayer' as the determining factor for travel status in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa who said,

‘I heard Al-Rezaasws saying: ‘When the sun (starts to) decline and you are inside the city, and you are intending the journey, so pray complete (Salāt). But when you go out after the midday, so shorten Al-Asr (Salāt)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from al-‘Ala’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ who has said the following:

“I once heard al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘At Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime) if you are in a city and want to travel, if you go out after Zawal perform al-‘Asr Salah in the reduced form.’”
